SL6502CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/6502/SL6502CPU.sleela)

SL6502CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SL6502CPU — a runnable model of the MOS 6502: an 8-bit accumulator machine with X/Y index registers, a stack pointer, and the N V - B D I Z C status flags. It extends SLCPURuntime, so register storage, memory, the ALU, and the fetch-decode-execute loop are inherited; this file supplies the 6502's registers and an instruction decoder. Instruction model (one word per instruction: op in bits 8..15, operand in bits 0..7) — a compact teaching encoding, not the byte-exact 6502 opcode map, sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a model for further .sleela inputs: LDA#imm, LDX#imm, LDY#imm, STA abs, LDA abs, ADC#imm, SBC#imm, INX, INY, TAX, TAY, JMP abs, BEQ rel, BNE rel, BRK(halt), NOP. decode() routes arithmetic through the inherited ALU (so flags are real) and can also lower the stream onto the secondary VM via the inherited emit*(). Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SL65C816CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/wdc-65c816/SL65C816CPU.sleela)

SL65C816CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SL65C816CPU — a runnable model of the WDC 65C816. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the WDC 65C816 register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SL68000CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/motorola-68000/SL68000CPU.sleela)

SL68000CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SL68000CPU — a runnable model of the Motorola 68000: a 16/32-bit CISC with eight data registers D0..D7 and eight address registers A0..A7 (A7 is the stack pointer), plus the X N Z V C condition codes. It extends SLCPURuntime and adds the 68000 register set, a decoder, and the effective-address / bus-arbitration hooks the skeleton named. Instruction model (op in high byte, then a 4-bit dst and 4-bit src selector or an immediate in the low byte): MOVE Dn,Dm / MOVEQ #imm,Dn / MOVE Dn,(An) / MOVE (An),Dn / ADD Dn,Dm / SUB Dn,Dm / ADDQ #imm,Dn / LEA #imm,An / JMP abs / BEQ / BNE / RTS(halt) / NOP. Compact teaching encoding, enough to run the CPU and model further .sleela inputs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLAdder #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLAdder.sleela)

SLAdder class

Defines SLAdder — an N-bit ripple-carry adder built from a chain of full adders. This is the arithmetic heart of the ALU: it adds two machine words bit-by-bit, propagating carry from the least significant bit to the most significant, and reports an overflow/carry-out. The ripple-carry structure is the textbook adder; faster CPUs use carry-lookahead or carry-select variants (documented in CPU.md), but the semantics are identical and this models the canonical case. Family: cpu. Composes SLFullAdder over a word width.

SLALU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLALU.sleela)

SLALU class

Defines SLALU — the Arithmetic Logic Unit. It is the CPU's calculator: given two operand words and an operation selector, it computes a result and sets condition flags (zero, negative, carry, overflow). It uses SLAdder for add/subtract (subtraction via two's-complement add) and gate-level logic for the bitwise operations. Operations: ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, SHL, SHR, CMP, PASS. Flags follow the usual CPU status register convention. Family: cpu. Composes SLAdder; pure Sleela arithmetic.

SLAMDEPYCCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/amd-epyc/SLAMDEPYCCPU.sleela)

SLAMDEPYCCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLAMDEPYCCPU — a runnable model of the AMD EPYC (Zen x86-64). It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the AMD EPYC (Zen x86-64) register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLAMDThreadripperPlatform #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/amd-threadripper/SLAMDThreadripperPlatform.sleela)

SLAMDThreadripperPlatform class

Defines SLAMDThreadripperPlatform — the ancillary, board-level operating point for the AMD Ryzen Threadripper 9000 (Zen 5 "Shimada Peak") family: the DDR5-6400 memory timings, the actual Vcore / Vsoc / Vddq supply rails in millivolts, and the HEDT (TRX50, 4-channel) vs PRO WX (WRX90, 8-channel) board topology. Where SLAMDThreadripperCPU is the runnable core, this class carries the "everything around the core" the shared expert-timing layer (SLRamTiming / SLVoltageRail) needs to characterize a real rig. Nothing here is invented: DDR5's I/O rail is 1.1 V (1100 mV) and the roster runs DDR5-6400 (JEDEC ~CL46); the Zen 5 core/SoC rails use AMD's documented nominal/limit points. Each getter hands back a configured object ready to drop into an SLTimingProfile or an SLExecutorBuild. Family: cpu. Composes SLRamTiming, SLVoltageRail, SLMotherboard, SLMemoryModule (via SLComponentCatalog); partners SLAMDThreadripperCPU.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
vcoreSLVoltageRail vcore()Vcore: Zen 5 core rail. Nominal ~1.20 V, safe window ~0.95–1.45 V.
vsocSLVoltageRail vsoc()Vsoc: SoC / memory-controller rail. AMD caps SoC at ~1.30 V; nominal ~1.20 V.
vddqSLVoltageRail vddq()Vddq: DDR5 I/O rail. DDR5 standard is 1.1 V (1100 mV), window ~1.067–1.166 V.
ddr5_6400TimingSLRamTiming ddr5_6400Timing(String channelName)An SLRamTiming configured for one DDR5-6400 channel at JEDEC primaries (CL46-46-46, tRAS 104, tRC 150, 2T), riding the Vddq rail. tRAS and tRC satisfy the honored() invariants (tRAS >= tRCD+CL, tRC >= tRAS+tRP).
hedtBoardSLMotherboard hedtBoard()HEDT board: sTR5 + TRX50, 4-channel DDR5, up to 88 PCIe 5.0 lanes.
proBoardSLMotherboard proBoard()Workstation board: sTR5 + WRX90, 8-channel DDR5, up to 128 PCIe 5.0 lanes.
hedtMemorySLMemoryModule hedtMemory(int capMiBPerModule)4-channel DDR5-6400 populated for the HEDT platform; capMiBPerModule is the per-DIMM capacity (e.g. 32768 for 32 GiB modules -> 128 GiB across 4).
proMemorySLMemoryModule proMemory(int capMiBPerModule)8-channel DDR5-6400 populated for the PRO WX platform.
pcie5x16SLSystemBus pcie5x16()PCIe 5.0 x16 system bus, as both Threadripper platforms carry.

SLARMCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/arm/SLARMCPU.sleela)

SLARMCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLARMCPU — a runnable model of a 32-bit ARM (A32-style): 16 registers R0..R15 (R13 SP, R14 LR, R15 PC) and the N Z C V flags in a CPSR. It extends SLCPURuntime and adds the ARM register set, condition-code evaluation, a decoder for a compact data-processing / load-store / branch encoding, and the exception / banked-register hooks the skeleton named. Instruction model (cond in bits 28..31, op in 20..27, rd in 16..19, rn in 12..15, operand2 in 0..11): MOV / ADD / SUB / CMP / LDR / STR / B / BL / SWI(exception+halt) / NOP. All instructions are conditionally executed via cond, as on ARM. Compact teaching encoding, enough to run the CPU and host further .sleela inputs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLAssembler #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLAssembler.sleela)

SLAssembler class

Defines SLAssembler — a tiny assembler that turns instruction mnemonics (from SLInstructionSet) and operands into encoded words appended to an SLProgram. It is the convenience layer programs are written through: emit(opcode, rd, rs, imm) encodes one instruction via SLInstruction. This lets a Sleela program for the Sleela CPU be authored in Sleela source, assembled into an SLProgram image, and then loaded by the OS. Family: cpu. Composes SLInstructionSet, SLInstruction, SLProgram.

SLBootloader #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLBootloader.sleela)

SLBootloader class

Defines SLBootloader — the firmware/boot sequence that runs on the CPU's boot core after power-on. It reads the kernel image from the boot disk into main memory, sets the boot core's entry point to the kernel, and hands off control. This is the bridge from bare hardware (SLCPU) to the OS (SLKernel). Family: cpu. Composes SLCPU, SLDiskDriver, SLRAM.

SLBus #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLBus.sleela)

SLBus class

Defines SLBus — the shared wiring that moves words between CPU components (registers, ALU, memory, I/O). A bus has an address lane, a data lane, and a control lane, plus a width. It models a single in-flight transfer and counts traffic; arbitration between masters is handled by the control unit that drives it. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela interconnect.

SLBusTiming #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLBusTiming.sleela)

SLBusTiming class

Defines SLBusTiming — the careful, nameful timing + variable clock speed of one interconnect (front-side / memory / peripheral bus). A bus here is not assumed to "just work" at a frequency: its clock is a VARIABLE speed with a floor and a ceiling the operator may dial between, and three named SLTiming budgets (address, data, control) are checked against the period that frequency implies. Bus timing is given special care — this is the class the thesis "timing issues for buses shall be careful and nameful" lives in — so the data-strobe path carries its own name and reason and the whole bus reports whether it is honored at the dialed speed. It rides on an SLVoltageRail: the achievable clock ceiling scales with the rail's effective (settled, under-load) voltage, so under-volting a bus lowers the speed it can be trusted at rather than silently corrupting it. Family: cpu. Composes SLTiming and SLVoltageRail; partners SLBus/SLClock.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLCache #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCache.sleela)

SLCache class

Defines SLCache — a CPU cache level (L1/L2/L3) sitting between a core and main memory. It models the properties that matter for behavior: total size, line size, associativity, and the hit/miss statistics that drive the memory hierarchy. On a miss it falls through to a backing SLRAM (or a slower cache level). This is a behavioral model: it tracks a modeled hit rate and forwards misses; the exact line contents live in the backing SLRAM below the bridge. Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM as its backing store.

SLCircuit #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCircuit.sleela)

SLCircuit class

Defines SLCircuit, a named combinational circuit built from gates. It is the organizing abstraction one level above SLGate: a circuit has a name, a declared gate/transistor budget, and tracks propagation so higher components (adders, decoders, the ALU) can describe themselves as circuits. Modern CPUs are hierarchies of circuits (standard cells -> functional blocks -> units -> cores). This class models that hierarchy at the Sleela-source layer: it counts constituent gates and composes sub-circuits, which lets the whole design report a transistor-order estimate. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela structure.

SLClipperCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/clipper/SLClipperCPU.sleela)

SLClipperCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLClipperCPU — a runnable model of the Fairchild Clipper. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the Fairchild Clipper register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLClockPolicy #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLClockPolicy.sleela)

SLClockPolicy class

Defines SLClockPolicy — how fast a Sleela CPU model runs. It carries the CPU's own spec clock (its rated MHz), a base-clock × multiplier decomposition (as real CPUs expose for overclocking), and a stability ceiling. A model runs at its spec clock by default; a user may overclock it by raising the multiplier or the base clock, up to the rated stability limit — beyond which the policy reports it as unstable. The effective MHz feeds performance accounting (how many model cycles a workload's instruction budget corresponds to) and the PERFECT.CONSEQUENCE speed/feasibility model: overclocking raises effective throughput linearly with the clock until the stability ceiling. Family: cpu. Composed by SLCPURuntime; refines SLClock.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLComponentCatalog #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLComponentCatalog.sleela)

SLComponentCatalog class

Defines SLComponentCatalog — the parts bin. It hands back ready-configured, real-world-spec'd components a user picks to build a Sleela executor: memory modules (DRAM through DDR5), storage (floppy, MFM HDD, SATA SSD, NVMe), optical drives (CD/DVD/Blu-ray), and system buses (ISA/PCI/AGP/PCIe). SLControlUnit class

Defines SLControlUnit — the conductor of a CPU core. It drives the fetch-decode-execute cycle for the full SLInstructionSet: fetch the instruction at the program counter, decode it, route operands through the register file, ALU, and the hardware stack (SLStack), write results back, update the program counter (sequential, branch, call, or return), and set the status flags. This models a classic single-cycle control unit with a real call/stack protocol: CALL pushes the return address and jumps; RET pops it; PUSH/POP move words to and from the stack. That protocol is what makes the ISA a viable lowering target for compiled C/C++/Java/Sleela (function calls, locals, spills). Pipelining/out-of-order are described in CPU.md; the observable semantics here are the same. Family: cpu. Composes decoder, register file, ALU, PC, status, RAM, and stack.

SLCore #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCore.sleela)

SLCore class

Defines SLCore — a single execution core: one control unit, its register file, ALU, program counter, status register, L1 cache, and interrupt controller, all driven by a clock. A modern CPU is several of these cores on one die; SLCPU composes them. assemble() wires the sub-units together so the core is ready to fetch from a shared RAM. tick() advances one clock cycle (one instruction in this single-cycle model). Family: cpu. Composes the Layer-0/1/2 components into a runnable core.

SLCortexMCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/cortex-m/SLCortexMCPU.sleela)

SLCortexMCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLCortexMCPU — a runnable model of the ARM Cortex-M. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the ARM Cortex-M register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCPU.sleela)

SLCPU class

Defines SLCPU — a complete multi-core processor package: a set of execution cores sharing main memory and a last-level (L3) cache, plus identifying metadata (vendor, model, core count, clock). This is the top of the hardware stack — the chip the operating system boots on. It models a typical Intel/AMD-style arrangement: N cores, private L1/L2 per core (L1 lives in SLCore), a shared L3, and one coherent main memory. Up to 8 cores are wired as fields (SLeeLa surface has no arrays). Family: cpu. Composes SLCore, SLCache, SLRAM.

SLCPUCatalog #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCPUCatalog.sleela)

SLCPUCatalog class

Defines SLCPUCatalog — the by-name front door to the CPU roster. Where SLHardwareRegistry catalogs memory/SSD/HDD/USB/GPU parts by name, this is the missing CPU family: a registry of the runnable SL<ARCH>CPU models so a caller can pick a processor by key (e.g. "6502", "arm", "riscv", "x86", "ps5", "xbox-series-x") instead of hard-coding `new SL6502CPU()`. Each entry records a stable key, a human label, the architecture family, the rated spec clock (MHz) and data-path width, so a fleet can be assembled from the roster and its performance accounted. The catalog hands back a configured, bring-up-ready SLCPURuntime via make(key); list()/keys() enumerate the roster for a chooser UI or a fleet runner. Family: cpu. Selects/instantiates models that extend SLCPURuntime; consumed by SLCPUFleet and any "choose a CPU" surface.

SLCPUFleet #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCPUFleet.sleela)

SLCPUFleet class

Defines SLCPUFleet — a selected roster of CPUs run as a group to produce NET RESULTS. Where SLCPURuntime.runWorkload() runs one program on one CPU and returns a single observable, a fleet selects several models from the SLCPUCatalog, runs a workload (or a workload set) across all of them, and AGGREGATES the per-CPU outcomes into a net-results scoreboard: total and effective throughput (scaled by each CPU's clock policy), admitted vs. rejected counts, the fastest/slowest member, and a per-member line. This is the "simulate a real world with net results" surface — the world is the set of heterogeneous machines, the net result is the aggregate of running real work on them. Family: cpu. Composes SLCPUCatalog + SLCPURuntime + SLWorkload/SLCPUResource.

SLCPUResource #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCPUResource.sleela)

SLCPUResource class

Defines SLCPUResource — a resource grant assigned to a workload running on a CPU. It is the unit of resource assignment: how much memory (words) the workload may address, how many instructions it may retire (instruction budget / time-slice), its scheduling priority, and whether it may use I/O and privileged services. A CPU admits a workload only if its model can satisfy the grant, then enforces it while the workload runs. This is what lets many workloads share one CPU model predictably: each gets a bounded, explicit slice of the machine, and the CPU accounts usage against it. Family: cpu. Composed by SLWorkload; enforced by SLCPURuntime.

runByOpcodesint runByOpcodes(int[] program, int at, int budget)(1) Run a native instruction-word program through the opcode loop. The program is an int[] of packed instruction words (as a model's assembler helper produces); it is loaded from `at`, the entry point is set, and the fetch-decode-execute loop runs within `budget`. Returns opcodes retired.
runByOpcodesint runByOpcodes(int[] program, int budget)No description in source.
runByEquivalenceint runByEquivalence(SLWorkload work)(2) Run the code of an assumed other process by function-call equivalence: the workload is compiled and mapped (SLOpcodeMap) to the equivalent opcode / service-call stream on this CPU, then executed within its grant. This is a first-class, honestly-named view of the shared workload path (runWorkload). Returns the observable output, or -1 if the workload was not admitted.
opcodeObservableint opcodeObservable()The observable result left by the OPCODE path. A native instruction loop leaves its result in architecture-defined state (a register or a memory cell), NOT on the lowering substrate -- so the base reads register 0 as the conventional result slot. A model whose result lands elsewhere (e.g. the 6502's accumulator) overrides this to name its own result location, so the basis comparison stays honest rather than assuming a fixed convention.
basisHoldsboolean basisHolds(int[] opcodeProgram, int opcodeBudget,Does this CPU run by both? The basis holds when the SAME computation, run by opcodes and by function-call equivalence, yields the SAME observable. `opcodeProgram` is the native-opcode form left in opcodeObservable(); `equivalentWork` is the assumed-other-process form whose observable is its printed output. `expected` is the agreed result both must produce (callers supply it because the two paths observe different surfaces -- a register vs. a printed value -- so equivalence means "both equal the intended result", not "both read the same physical slot"). Returns true iff both agree with it.
runsByBothboolean runsByBoth()A model advertises that running by both mechanisms is part of its basis. Always true for an SLCPURuntime-derived model: both the opcode loop and the equivalence pipeline are inherited here. Subclasses do not re-implement it; they inherit the capability by extending this runtime.

SLCpuTiming #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLCpuTiming.sleela)

SLCpuTiming class

Defines SLCpuTiming — the expert core-timing settings of a CPU: the actual core clock (variable, with floor/ceiling), the Vcore rail it runs on, and the per-stage pipeline budgets (fetch, decode, execute, writeback) stated as named SLTiming paths. Rather than assume a core "just runs" at its advertised frequency, the critical path (the slowest stage) determines the real maximum clock, and dialing above what the stage budgets and the settled Vcore can honor is refused. This is the expert surface for CPU timing: a tuner states measured stage delays and a Vcore operating point, and the class reports the honest ceiling, the critical stage by name, and whether the dialed point is honored. Family: cpu. Composes SLTiming and SLVoltageRail; partners SLCore/SLClock.

SLDeviceDriver #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLDeviceDriver.sleela)

SLDeviceDriver class

Defines SLDeviceDriver — the base class for all device drivers. A driver is the software contract between the OS and a hardware device: it owns the device's I/O port(s), exposes a uniform lifecycle (probe, attach, open, read/write, close, detach), and fields the device's interrupt. The kernel talks to devices only through drivers. Concrete drivers (console, disk, keyboard, network) extend this and override the transfer methods. Family: cpu. Composes SLIOBus; base of the driver hierarchy.

SLDMAController #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLDMAController.sleela)

SLDMAController class

Defines SLDMAController — a direct memory access engine. When the DMA option is enabled, a program (or a device) can move a block of words between memory regions WITHOUT the CPU copying each word in its fetch-decode-execute loop: the controller does the transfer directly over SLRAM. It models independent channels, source/destination/length descriptors, a direction/mode, and completion status, like a real DMA controller (8237 / modern scatter-gather). This is the "direct DMA option": a Sleela executor that enables it can hand a bulk move to the DMA engine at any point the program needs it, freeing the CPU. Transfers are bounded by the backing SLRAM and accounted for. Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM. Enabled via the DMA option on SLCPURuntime / SLVM.

SLDreamcastCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/sega-dreamcast/SLDreamcastCPU.sleela)

SLDreamcastCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLDreamcastCPU — a runnable model of the Sega Dreamcast (SH-4). It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the Sega Dreamcast (SH-4) register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. SLExecutorBuild #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLExecutorBuild.sleela)

SLExecutorBuild class

Defines SLExecutorBuild — a user-assembled Sleela executor: a CPU model (SLCPURuntime / SL<ARCH>CPU) running at its spec clock (or overclocked) plus the components the user picked from SLComponentCatalog — a motherboard, a memory module, a primary storage device, an optional optical drive, and a system bus. SLFlipFlop #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLFlipFlop.sleela)

SLFlipFlop class

Defines SLFlipFlop — an edge-triggered 1-bit storage element (a D flip-flop). Unlike a latch, it captures its input only on a clock edge, which is what makes synchronous CPUs possible: all registers update together on the rising edge of the clock. Built from a master/slave pair of latches. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela state; clocked.

SLFrontend #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLFrontend.sleela)

SLFrontend class

Defines SLFrontend — the base class for every language frontend. A frontend turns program source in one language into the common SLIR, which the shared backend (SLLowering) then compiles to machine code for the SLInstructionSet. Concrete frontends exist for C, C++, Java, and Sleela. The contract is deliberately the same one real toolchains use: a frontend is responsible for its language's lexing, parsing, and semantic lowering to a common IR; everything after the IR (optimization, register allocation, code emission) is language-neutral and shared. Family: cpu. Base of the frontend hierarchy; composes SLIR.

SLFrontendC #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLFrontendC.sleela)

SLFrontendC class extends SLFrontend

Defines SLFrontendC — the C-language frontend. It lowers C translation units to the common SLIR: declarations become memory/stack slots, expressions become IR temporaries and arithmetic ops, function calls become IR_PARAM/IR_CALL, and `return` becomes IR_RET. The shared backend then compiles the IR to machine code for the SLInstructionSet. SCOPE NOTE: a full C compiler (preprocessor, the entire type system, the standard library) is far beyond one class; this frontend models the real C-to-IR lowering contract and demonstrates a complete lowering for a small C function (int add3(void){ return 2+3; } then write+exit). Extending it to full C means growing parse() into a complete C parser — the IR and backend below it do not change. This mirrors how clang targets LLVM IR. Family: cpu. Extends SLFrontend.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

initvoid init(String path)No description in source.
lowerSLIR lower()Model lowering of the CANONICAL equivalence program: int main(void){ int x = 2 + 3; write(1, &x, 1); return 0; } Every frontend in the family lowers this same computation (x = 2 + 3, write x, exit) so that reducing all four to the Sleela opcode substrate yields the identical observable result — the operational statement of 1:1 Turing effect (see SLTuringBridge). The language-specific lowering shapes (C automatic storage, C++ objects, JVM bytecode) differ; the computed value does not.

SLFrontendCpp #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLFrontendCpp.sleela)

SLFrontendCpp class extends SLFrontendC

Defines SLFrontendCpp — the C++ frontend. It extends the C frontend's lowering with the C++-specific constructs that still reduce to the same common SLIR: an object's method call lowers to a function call whose first IR_PARAM is the `this` pointer; a constructor lowers to an allocation plus an initializer call; virtual dispatch lowers to a vtable load (IR_LOAD) followed by an indirect IR_CALL. SCOPE NOTE: templates, overload resolution, exceptions, and the STL are a full C++ front-end's job and are out of scope for one class; this models the canonical C++-to-IR lowerings (this-pointer, construction, virtual dispatch) and demonstrates one complete lowering. The IR and backend are unchanged — exactly how clang++ shares LLVM with clang. Family: cpu. Extends SLFrontendC (C++ is a superset lowering).

SLFrontendJava #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLFrontendJava.sleela)

SLFrontendJava class extends SLFrontend

Defines SLFrontendJava — the Java frontend. Java is already compiled to JVM bytecode by javac, so this frontend lowers from that stack-based bytecode to the common SLIR: bytecode locals become IR temporaries, the operand stack is linearized into three-address IR, invokestatic/invokevirtual become IR_PARAM/IR_CALL, and System.out writes lower to a syscall. SCOPE NOTE: a full classfile reader (constant pool, all ~200 bytecodes, verification) is a project of its own; this models the canonical bytecode-to-IR lowering and demonstrates one complete lowering. The IR and backend are shared with the other languages. Family: cpu. Extends SLFrontend.

It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the Nintendo GameCube (Gekko / PowerPC) register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLGate #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGate.sleela)

SLGate class

Defines SLGate, a single Boolean logic gate — the foundational primitive of the SLeeLa CPU. Every circuit, adder, register, and ALU is ultimately composed from gates, so the whole CPU is Sleela source that bottoms out here. A gate takes one or two 1-bit inputs (0 or 1) and produces one 1-bit output according to its kind. Kinds: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR, BUF. NAND/NOR are universal — any logic can be built from them alone — which is why real silicon favors them; this class exposes them directly. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela logic; no native bridge needed at this layer.

SLGPUDevice #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGPUDevice.sleela)

SLGPUDevice class

Defines SLGPUDevice — a graphics/compute processor a Sleela executor can offload work to when the GPU option is enabled. It models the real spec that matters for compute: a number of compute units each running many lanes (SIMT), a core clock, and a block of VRAM (its own SLRAM). A kernel is a canonical-opcode program dispatched across a grid of lanes; the device executes it against VRAM. A native-access path (nativeDispatch) crosses the explicit bridge to a real host GPU (CUDA/OpenCL/Metal/Vulkan) when available, mirroring the native engine's bridge discipline. This is the "native GPU access" option: a program that needs the GPU — SIMD math, large parallel maps — asks the device to run a kernel, rather than grinding it on the scalar CPU. Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM (VRAM) and SLSleelaVM (per-lane kernel engine). Enabled via the GPU option on SLCPURuntime / SLVM.

SLGuestBlockDevice #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestBlockDevice.sleela)

SLGuestBlockDevice class extends SLGuestDevice

Defines SLGuestBlockDevice — a virtual block storage device (virtio-blk-style) backed by a host SLHardDrive. The guest kernel programs a block number and buffer address, issues a read or write, and the device performs the transfer and raises its IRQ on completion. This is how a guest OS loads its root filesystem and pages to/from disk. MMIO registers: 0 = block number, 1 = guest buffer address, 2 = command (1 read, 2 write), 3 = status (RO). Completion raises the device IRQ. Family: cpu. Extends SLGuestDevice; composes SLHardDrive.

SLGuestDevice #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestDevice.sleela)

SLGuestDevice class

Defines SLGuestDevice — the base class for virtual devices the hypervisor exposes to a guest VM. A guest kernel talks to these through memory-mapped registers (guest MMIO addresses); a register access that falls in a device's window is a VM-exit the hypervisor routes to the device model. This is step 3 of the OS-VM roadmap: the minimum device surface a guest OS expects (timer, interrupt controller, console, block device). Each device owns an MMIO base/size and read()/write() register handlers plus an optional interrupt line it can raise into the guest. Family: cpu. Base of the guest device hierarchy.

SLGuestDeviceBus #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestDeviceBus.sleela)

SLGuestDeviceBus class

Defines SLGuestDeviceBus — the virtual device bus the hypervisor presents to a guest VM. It holds the guest's devices (timer, console, block device), routes a guest MMIO access to the device that owns the address, and aggregates device interrupts into the guest's interrupt controller. This is the "chipset" of the guest machine (step 3 of the OS-VM roadmap). MMIO dispatch: a guest read/write to a device-owned address is a VM-exit the hypervisor services by calling the owning device's register handler. IRQ aggregation: after a tick, any device with a raised line is posted to the guest interrupt controller for the guest kernel to service. Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestTimer/Console/BlockDevice and SLInterruptController.

SLGuestExecutable #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestExecutable.sleela)

SLGuestExecutable class

Defines SLGuestExecutable — a simple on-disk executable format for guest programs (a miniature ELF). It has a fixed header (magic, version, entry offset, opcode count) followed by an opcode section (op+arg pairs). A compiled SLGuestProgram can be *serialized* to this format and written to the guest filesystem; the loader can later *read it back from disk* and load it into the guest substrate — so programs come from storage, not only from inline compilation. On-disk layout (one word per slot in the backing store): [0] magic 0x5345584c ("SEXL") [1] version [2] entry [3] opcode-count [4..] interleaved op,arg,op,arg,... Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM (image bytes), SLGuestFileSystem (storage), SLSleelaVM (load target).

SLGuestFileSystem #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestFileSystem.sleela)

SLGuestFileSystem class

Defines SLGuestFileSystem — a minimal in-guest filesystem over the guest block device. It presents named files (a flat directory) backed by block storage, with an open-file table of descriptors supporting sequential read/write by byte. The guest kernel's syscall layer (SLGuestSyscall) uses it for open/read/write/close; the loader can read program images from it. This is a guest-side analogue of the host SLFileSystem but scoped to a guest VM and reached through the guest block device (SLGuestBlockDevice). Files are identified by an integer name/handle (the guest passes an interned id) to fit the integer-only syscall ABI; a small fixed directory (8 files) and fd table (8 descriptors) are modeled (SLeeLa surface has no arrays). Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestBlockDevice.

SLGuestInit #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestInit.sleela)

SLGuestInit class

Defines SLGuestInit — the guest's init process (PID 1). After the guest kernel boots, init loads user programs (SLGuestProgram) into the guest substrate and hands each to the guest scheduler as a task (SLGuestTask). This is how a guest OS goes from "kernel running" to "running user processes": init is the first task and the parent of the rest. Models the Unix init contract: PID 1 is spawned by the kernel, then spawns the system's initial programs; the timer-driven scheduler multitasks them. Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestLinux, SLGuestProgram, SLGuestTask, SLSleelaVM.

execSLGuestTask exec(String name, String sourcePath, int langId)Compile a program from source and spawn it (exec-style convenience).
execFromImageSLGuestTask execFromImage(String name, SLGuestExecutable image)Load a program FROM DISK: given a prepared executable image, load it into the guest substrate and admit it as a task. This is the "run a program from the filesystem" path (as opposed to inline compilation via exec()).
installAndExecSLGuestTask installAndExec(String name, String sourcePath, int langId, int fileId)Compile a program, serialize it to the on-disk executable format, write it to the guest filesystem under `fileId`, then load it back from disk and spawn it — the full compile -> install -> load-from-disk -> run cycle.
execIntoint execInto(SLGuestTask task, int progId, int srcId, int langId)execve support: replace an EXISTING task's image with a freshly compiled program, loaded into the shared guest substrate, and repoint that task's resume IP at the new image's entry. Unlike spawn()/exec(), this does NOT create a new task — the caller keeps its tid and scheduling slot but now runs different code, exactly as Unix execve() replaces the process image in place. The program is resolved through the same toolchain; progId/srcId are modeled identifiers the kernel maps to a source path/name. Returns the new entry index, or -1 on failure.
execNameString execName(int progId)Map a modeled program/source identifier to a name/path. Kept trivial and deterministic so the exec path is reproducible in the model; a real kernel would resolve these from the execve() argument vector.
execSourcePathString execSourcePath(int srcId)No description in source.
launchShellSLGuestShell launchShell()Launch the guest shell as init's first child: build a shell bound to the kernel's syscall table and admit it as a task (the first interactive user program after boot). Returns the shell object so a driver can feed it commands.
forkExecWaitDemoint forkExecWaitDemo(int childLang)Demonstrate the full process-creation cycle through the real syscall ABI: spawn a base task, then from that task's context fork a child, execve the child onto a freshly compiled image, let the child exit, and wait() to reap it. Returns the reaped child's tid (>0) on success, or a negative error. This is the end-to-end fork/exec/wait path a Unix shell relies on.

SLGuestKernelBuilder #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestKernelBuilder.sleela)

SLGuestKernelBuilder class

Defines SLGuestKernelBuilder — builds a bootable guest kernel image by running kernel source through the real toolchain: a language frontend (SLCompilerDriver) lowers it to the register ISA, SLOpcodeMap reduces that to canonical SLeeLa opcodes, and the result is packaged as an SLGuestKernelImage. This is step 4 of the OS-VM roadmap: the guest boots a GENUINELY COMPILED kernel instead of a hand-written opcode stub. Because the kernel is compiled through the same frontend/IR/opcode pipeline as user programs, the guest kernel can in principle be written in any of the supported languages (C/C++/Java/Sleela) — a direct consequence of the 1:1 Turing-effect mapping (SLTuringBridge). SCOPE NOTE: this builds a small CUSTOM kernel, not upstream Linux. Family: cpu. Composes SLCompilerDriver, SLOpcodeMap, SLSleelaVM, SLInstructionSet, SLSystemCall, SLGuestKernelImage.

SLGuestLinux #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestLinux.sleela)

SLGuestLinux class

Defines SLGuestLinux — a Linux-style guest operating system that boots inside an SLGuestVM on the Sleela CPU. It models the Linux boot and runtime surface the hypervisor must support: a boot protocol (load kernel image + initrd into the guest window and jump to the entry), a Linux-style syscall ABI (write/read/open/close/exit/mmap/fork/execve as numbers), and the init handoff (PID 1). SCOPE NOTE — important: this is an ARCHITECTURAL MODEL of running a Linux-like guest, not the real Linux kernel. It defines the boot sequence, the syscall numbers the guest issues, and how those become VM-exits the hypervisor emulates. Running the actual upstream Linux kernel would require a full hardware-virtualization CPU and device model (far beyond this library). The value here is a faithful, composable model of the layering: SLCPU -> SleelaOS -> SLHypervisor -> SLGuestVM -> SLGuestLinux -> guest programs. Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestVM; booted by SLHypervisor.

GUEST_EMULATEDstatic final int GUEST_EMULATED = 100Translate a guest Linux syscall number to the host SleelaOS syscall the hypervisor emulates it with (the VM-exit handler's job). Host-syscall mapping constants (SLSystemCall surface: write/read/open/close/ exit/spawn/yield = 0..6). Process creation is modeled thus: a guest fork() leans on the host's SYS_SPAWN primitive, while execve()/wait() have no host equivalent and are serviced entirely in-guest (SLGuestSyscall against the guest scheduler/process table). The actual in-guest routing happens in SLGuestVM.handleExit() off the OP_SPAWN/OP_JOINALL service opcodes; emulateSyscall() is the ABI-classification view, so it returns the GUEST_EMULATED tag (not a host syscall number) for those two to make the "no host delegate" distinction explicit to callers that classify a syscall.

SLGuestPipe #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestPipe.sleela)

SLGuestPipe class

Defines SLGuestPipe — a unidirectional byte FIFO between guest tasks, the classic Unix pipe. One task writes bytes to the write end; another reads them from the read end in order. A read on an empty pipe signals "would block" (the kernel can block the reader); a write to a full pipe signals back-pressure. This is the first inter-process communication primitive for the guest OS. Backed by a ring buffer over SLRAM so the capacity is configurable. The guest syscall layer exposes pipe()/read()/write()/close() over these. Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM.

SLGuestScheduler #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestScheduler.sleela)

SLGuestScheduler class

Defines SLGuestScheduler — the GUEST kernel's task scheduler, driven by the guest timer device. It holds the guest's runnable tasks and, on each timer IRQ (the preemption source), rotates the CPU to the next ready task (round-robin). This is what gives the guest OS preemptive multitasking on its own virtual hardware: the SLGuestTimer heartbeat is the scheduler tick. Up to 8 guest tasks (SLeeLa surface has no arrays). The scheduler is a guest- side analogue of the host SLScheduler, but it runs inside the VM and is clocked by the guest timer rather than the host timer. Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestTask; clocked by SLGuestTimer via the device bus.

SLGuestShell #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestShell.sleela)

SLGuestShell class

Defines SLGuestShell — a minimal interactive shell for the guest OS, spawned by init (SLGuestInit) as its first child. It reads a command line, parses the leading word as a builtin, and executes it through the guest syscall ABI: writing output to the console, reading files from the guest filesystem, listing/inspecting tasks via the scheduler. This is the guest's first real user program — the thing a person "sees" after boot. Builtins: help, echo, ls, cat, ps, exit. Commands are issued as guest syscalls (write/read/open/close/getpid/exit), so the shell exercises the full user->kernel boundary built in the previous steps. Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestSyscall (its only kernel interface).

SLGuestSignal #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestSignal.sleela)

SLGuestSignal class

Defines SLGuestSignal — asynchronous signal delivery to guest tasks (the Unix signal model). A task (or the kernel) raises a signal number against a target task; the target has a pending-signal set and a per-signal disposition (default, ignore, or a handler entry point). On the next scheduling point the kernel delivers the highest-priority pending signal: it either applies the default action (e.g. terminate on KILL/TERM), ignores it, or vectors the task to its handler. Models up to 16 signal numbers with a pending bitset and dispositions held per target task id (a small fixed table; SLeeLa surface has no arrays). Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestScheduler for delivery/termination effects.

SLGuestSyscall #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestSyscall.sleela)

SLGuestSyscall class

Defines SLGuestSyscall — the guest kernel's system-call ABI and dispatcher. When a guest user program issues a syscall, the substrate takes a VM-exit; SLGuestVM routes it here, and this class emulates the requested service against the guest's devices (console), filesystem, scheduler, and task table, then returns a result the guest resumes with. This is the controlled user->kernel boundary a real OS exposes. ABI: a guest syscall carries a number plus up to three integer arguments (modeled as the exit payload + operand-stack values). The dispatcher returns an integer result (or a negative errno-style code), and reports control effects (exit/yield) so SLGuestVM can act on them. Family: cpu. Composes SLGuestDeviceBus, SLGuestFileSystem, SLGuestScheduler.

SLGuestTask #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestTask.sleela)

SLGuestTask class

Defines SLGuestTask — a unit of execution the GUEST kernel schedules (a guest thread / task control block). It is distinct from SLProcess (which the host OS schedules): this runs inside a guest VM, with its own guest entry point, saved guest-substrate instruction pointer, and run state. SLGuestTimer #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestTimer.sleela)

SLGuestTimer class extends SLGuestDevice

Defines SLGuestTimer — a programmable interval timer exposed to the guest. The guest kernel programs a reload value; each tick decrements a counter, and on expiry the timer raises its IRQ (the guest's scheduler tick / preemption source). This is the heartbeat a guest OS needs for timekeeping and preemptive multitasking. MMIO registers: 0 = reload value (RW), 1 = current count (RO), 2 = control (bit0 enable). IRQ fires on count reaching zero when enabled. Family: cpu. Extends SLGuestDevice.

SLGuestVM #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLGuestVM.sleela)

SLGuestVM class

Defines SLGuestVM — one guest virtual machine managed by the hypervisor. It presents a virtual CPU over a window of host memory (guest-physical addressing) and, crucially, EXECUTES the guest as a stream of canonical SLeeLa opcodes on an embedded SLSleelaVM substrate. Guest code is therefore run by the same Turing-complete engine as everything else in the model (step 1 of the OS-VM roadmap): the guest is not merely ticked and counted — its opcodes are actually dispatched. A guest TRAP/SYSCALL opcode is a VM-exit: the vCPU stops at that point, the hypervisor/guest-kernel emulates the operation, and the guest resumes. VM exits are recorded so the hypervisor can account for and service them. Guest address translation uses a real MMU (SLMMU, page tables + protection) when one is attached, falling back to a single base-offset window otherwise. Family: cpu. Composes SLCore, SLSleelaVM, SLRAM, SLMMU.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

entervoid enter()Enter the guest: put the substrate in hosted mode (service opcodes become VM-exits the hypervisor routes), record the translated entry on the vCPU.
runint run(int budget)Run the guest, driving the VM-exit loop (step 5): execute substrate opcodes until a VM-exit (a service opcode parks one) or HALT; route each exit to the device model / syscall emulation; resolve it and resume. Devices are ticked each round so the timer heartbeat advances and posts interrupts.
handleExitvoid handleExit(int opcode, int arg, int payload)Route a VM-exit from a service opcode to the guest syscall ABI (step b). Service opcodes are the guest's syscall surface: OP_PRINT is write(1, ch), and the OP_FILE* opcodes are open/read/write/close. When a kernel is attached, the exit is dispatched through its syscall table (which emulates the service against the guest console, filesystem, and scheduler); the result is pushed back for the guest to resume with. SYS_EXIT finishes the running task.
serviceOpcodeint serviceOpcode(int opcode, int arg, int payload)Route one service opcode to the guest syscall ABI and return the syscall result, applying the SYS_EXIT side effect (finish the running task). This is the shared routing used by handleExit(); exposing it lets the guest's process-creation path (OP_SPAWN fork/execve, OP_JOINALL wait) be driven and observed directly, so the opcode->syscall mapping is exercised end to end.
syscallNumberForint syscallNumberFor(int opcode, int arg, SLSleelaOpcode op, SLGuestSyscall sys)Map a service opcode to a guest syscall number. The process-creation family reuses the canonical substrate opcodes: OP_SPAWN is clone/exec (its arg selects fork vs. execve) and OP_JOINALL is wait.
syscallArg0int syscallArg0(int opcode, int arg, SLSleelaOpcode op, int payload)The first syscall argument (fd for I/O; progId for execve): OP_PRINT writes to stdout (fd 1); OP_SPAWN carries the exec program id as its stack payload, surfaced to execve as arg0.
syscallArg2int syscallArg2(int opcode, int arg, SLSleelaOpcode op)The third syscall argument (execve langId): recovered from OP_SPAWN's arg, which holds langId + 1 so that arg 0 can mean "plain fork".
deliverPendingInterruptsvoid deliverPendingInterrupts()Surface any device interrupts the guest PIC now has pending and deliver them to the guest kernel. A timer IRQ (line 0) drives the guest scheduler (step 6): the kernel preempts the running task and selects the next one, and the substrate resumes at that task's saved instruction pointer.
recordSyscallExitvoid recordSyscallExit()A guest syscall VM-exit: the guest kernel calls this when its code reaches a service point, so the hypervisor can emulate it against the host.

SLHardDrive #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLHardDrive.sleela)

SLHardDrive class

Defines SLHardDrive — persistent block storage (an HDD or SSD). It is the slowest, largest tier of the storage hierarchy and the device the OS boots from and loads programs out of. It presents a block interface (read/write by block number) and crosses the explicit VM/OS bridge to the native file-backed store. Models capacity in blocks, block size, media kind (spinning vs. solid-state), and I/O counters. Family: cpu. Native file-backed store via bridge.

SLI860CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/i860/SLI860CPU.sleela)

SLI860CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLI860CPU — a runnable model of the Intel i860. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the Intel i860 register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLInstruction #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLInstruction.sleela)

SLInstruction class

Defines SLInstruction — one decoded machine instruction: an opcode plus up to two register operands and an immediate/address field. This is the unit the fetch stage produces and the execute stage consumes. Encoding (modeled): [opcode][rd][rs][imm]. A real ISA packs these into fixed- or variable-width words; here they are fields for clarity. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela data.

SLInstructionSet #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLInstructionSet.sleela)

SLInstructionSet class

Defines SLInstructionSet — the CPU's instruction set architecture (ISA): the catalog of operations the control unit decodes and executes. This is a RISC-style ISA broad enough to be a lowering target for compiled C, C++, Java, and Sleela: load/store (immediate, register, and indexed addressing), full integer arithmetic/logic, compare, conditional and unconditional branches, a real call/return and stack protocol, I/O, system calls, and halt. It aligns with the canonical SLeeLa VM ISA in lib/vm/InstructionSet.sleela (OP_ADD, OP_JMP, OP_CALL, OP_RET, OP_HALT, ...). The multi-language frontends (SLFrontendC, SLFrontendCpp, SLFrontendJava, SLFrontendSleela) lower to the common IR (SLIR) which emits these opcodes. Each mnemonic has a stable numeric opcode; mnemonic<->code lookup is provided. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela ISA registry.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLIntelCeleronCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLIntelCeleronCPU — a runnable model of the Intel Celeron. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. SLIOTiming #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLIOTiming.sleela)

SLIOTiming class

Defines SLIOTiming — the expert timing settings for CONTROL of I/O: the handshake and transfer timing of a peripheral/port link. I/O is given the same careful, nameful treatment buses get, because an I/O link mixes an asynchronous device clock domain with the CPU's: the class states the link clock (variable), the setup/hold of the request/acknowledge handshake, the turnaround (bus direction reversal) time, and a recovery gap between transactions — each a named SLTiming budget. It also models the synchronizer latency crossing the device clock domain into the CPU domain, so I/O control timing is accounted honestly rather than assumed instant. The thesis "expert timings for control of I/O shall be careful and nameful" lives here: handshake, turnaround, and recovery each carry a name and reason, and the link reports whether a transaction is honored at the dialed speed. Family: cpu. Composes SLTiming and SLVoltageRail; partners SLIOBus/SLIOPort.

SLIR #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLIR.sleela)

SLIR class

Defines SLIR — a module of common intermediate representation: an ordered sequence of SLIRInstruction nodes plus a temporary-allocation counter and a label counter. Every language frontend (C, C++, Java, Sleela) produces an SLIR; the shared backend SLLowering consumes it. This is the single convergence point that makes the ISA genuinely multi-language. Backed by SLRAM for the node stream (SLeeLa surface has no arrays); nodes are stored by index and the lowering pass walks them in order. Family: cpu. Composes SLIRInstruction; the IR container.

SLIRInstruction #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLIRInstruction.sleela)

SLIRInstruction class

Defines SLIRInstruction — one instruction of the common intermediate representation (IR) that every language frontend lowers to. The IR is a small, language-neutral three-address form: an operation plus a destination temporary and up to two source operands (temporaries or immediates). SLLowering turns a stream of these into real machine code for the SLInstructionSet. A single IR shared by C, C++, Java, and Sleela is exactly how real multi- language toolchains work (e.g. LLVM IR behind clang/clang++/other frontends; a bytecode IR behind javac). This models that convergence point. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela IR node.

SLKernel #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLKernel.sleela)

SLKernel class

Defines SLKernel — the heart of the operating system. It owns the scheduler, memory manager, driver manager, syscall interface, and filesystem, and it runs on the CPU that the bootloader handed off to. The kernel installs its syscall handler and interrupt handlers, services syscalls from user programs, and drives preemptive multitasking via the timer interrupt. This is the "Sleela OS equivalent": a class-driven kernel built entirely from the /lib/cpu components, running on the Sleela-source CPU. Family: cpu. Composes the whole OS layer.

SLLatch #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLLatch.sleela)

SLLatch class

Defines SLLatch — a level-sensitive 1-bit storage element (an SR / gated-D latch). It is the most basic memory cell: when enabled, it captures the data input; otherwise it holds its stored bit. Flip-flops, registers, and SRAM cells are built up from latches. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela state.

SLLowering #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLLowering.sleela)

SLLowering class

Defines SLLowering — the shared compiler backend. It walks an SLIR module and emits real machine instructions (via SLAssembler) for the SLInstructionSet, performing a simple temporary-to-register allocation and two-pass label resolution. Because every language frontend produces the same SLIR, this one backend serves C, C++, Java, and Sleela — the ISA is multi-language because the backend is shared. Register convention: IR temporaries map to r1..r15 round-robin (r0 is the hardwired zero). Spilling to the stack for programs that exceed the register file is described in CPU.md and modeled by PUSH/POP; this pass handles the common small-function case directly. Family: cpu. Composes SLIR, SLAssembler, SLProgram, SLInstructionSet.

SLMachine #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLMachine.sleela)

SLMachine class

Defines SLMachine — the complete computer: it composes the entire /lib/cpu stack into one bootable system and demonstrates the full chain the library exists to express: gates -> adders/ALU -> registers/RAM/cache -> cores -> SLCPU (hardware) -> SLBootloader loads the kernel (boot) -> SLOperatingSystem / SLKernel comes up with drivers + scheduler (OS) -> SLAssembler builds a Sleela program (program) -> SLProgramLoader loads it as a process (load) -> SLKernel schedules and runs it on the Sleela CPU (run) This is the Sleela CPU built from Sleela source, booting a Sleela Class-Driven OS, which then loads and runs Sleela programs on top of it. Family: cpu. Top-level composition of the whole package.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
buildHardwarevoid buildHardware(String vendor, String model, int cores, int bits, int mhz)Build the hardware: main memory, boot disk, and a multi-core CPU.
bootvoid boot()Boot: firmware loads the kernel image, then the OS installs and comes up.
loadLanguageProgramSLProcess loadLanguageProgram(String path, int langId, String procName, int loadAddr)Compile and load a source program in any supported language, returning the spawned process. Language ids: 0 Sleela, 1 C, 2 C++, 3 Java.
runOnSubstrateint runOnSubstrate(int langId, String path, String name)Reduce a program in any supported language to the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate and execute it there, returning its printed result. This runs the program as a stream of the Turing-complete canonical opcodes — the common ground C/C++/Java/Sleela all share.
proveLanguageEquivalenceboolean proveLanguageEquivalence(String c, String cpp, String java, String sleela)Prove the four languages are 1:1 in Turing effect: identical observable result after each is reduced to the Sleela opcode substrate.
runLinuxGuestint runLinuxGuest(int guestEntry, int budget)Boot a Linux-style guest OS on top of this Sleela CPU via the hypervisor, and run it for a bounded number of guest instructions. Returns the guest instruction count executed. (Architectural model — see SLGuestLinux.)
runLinuxGuestFromSourceint runLinuxGuestFromSource(String kernelSourcePath, int langId, int guestEntry, int budget)Boot a Linux-style guest whose kernel is GENUINELY COMPILED from source in any supported language (C/C++/Java/Sleela) via the real toolchain (step 4), then run it. Returns the guest instruction count executed.
runLinuxGuestWithProgramsint runLinuxGuestWithPrograms(String kernelSrc, int kernelLang,Boot a guest, then have its init process (PID 1) load and spawn two user programs compiled from source (any supported language). The timer-driven scheduler then multitasks them. Returns the guest instruction count.
runLinuxGuestDiskProgramint runLinuxGuestDiskProgram(String kernelSrc, int kernelLang,Boot a guest, then compile a program, install it to the guest filesystem as an on-disk executable, load it back FROM DISK, and run it. Demonstrates the full compile -> install -> load-from-disk -> execute cycle. Returns the guest instruction count executed.
runLinuxGuestShellint runLinuxGuestShell(String kernelSrc, int kernelLang, int guestEntry)Boot a guest, launch its shell as init's first child, and run a short command script (each entry is a leading-char + arg pair). Returns the number of shell commands executed. Demonstrates boot -> init -> shell.
runLinuxGuestForkExecint runLinuxGuestForkExec(String kernelSrc, int kernelLang,Boot a guest, then exercise the full PROCESS-CREATION cycle — fork, execve, and wait — through the guest's real syscall ABI (SLGuestSyscall). init spawns a parent task, forks a child, execs the child onto a freshly compiled image, the child exits, and the parent reaps it with wait(). Returns the reaped child's tid (>0 on success). Demonstrates boot -> init -> fork/exec/wait: a Linux-style guest creating and reaping processes.
runLinuxGuestForkExecOpcodesint runLinuxGuestForkExecOpcodes(String kernelSrc, int kernelLang, int guestEntry)Same process-creation cycle, but driven through the guest's OPCODE path: the canonical service opcodes OP_SPAWN (fork) and OP_JOINALL (wait) are routed by SLGuestVM.serviceOpcode() -> syscallNumberFor() -> the syscall ABI, exactly as a guest program's VM-exits are. This exercises the opcode->syscall mapping (not just the syscall handlers). Returns the reaped child's tid (>0 on success).
buildBootDiskDriverSLDiskDriver buildBootDiskDriver()The bootloader needs a disk driver before the OS driver manager exists; build a minimal one bound to the boot drive.
loadDemoProgramSLProcess loadDemoProgram(int loadAddr)Author, assemble, load, and run a demonstration Sleela program: compute 2 + 3 into r1, print a character via SYS_WRITE, then exit.
powerOnAndRunint powerOnAndRun(int cores, int bits, int mhz, int rounds)Run the whole chain end to end: build -> boot -> load program -> run.
selectTimingSLTimingProfile selectTiming(int tier, String brandOrMedium)Select the machine's adjustable timing/voltage operating point for a given expertise tier (SLTimingClass.TIER_NOVICE/BASIC/ADVANCED/EXPERT) and brand or medium. The profile owns the actual voltages, the variable bus/core/IO clocks, and the expert CPU/RAM/I/O timings; it is sealed into a manifest that every program compiled through the loader's compiler then carries.
compileWithTimingSLProgram compileWithTiming(String path, int langId, String programName)Compile a program with the machine's selected timing profile stamped into the resulting .sleela image, so the VM/loader honor the declared operating point instead of assuming hardware quality. Returns the compiled program.
timingHonoredboolean timingHonored()Is the machine's selected operating point internally honored — every expert timing met on every rail at the dialed speeds, with the tier's headroom?

operatingSystemSLOperatingSystem operatingSystem()No description in source.

This file supplies the Sega Mega-CD (68000) register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLMemoryManager #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLMemoryManager.sleela)

SLMemoryManager class

Defines SLMemoryManager — the OS's physical/virtual memory manager. It carves main memory into pages, tracks which are free vs. allocated, and hands page-aligned regions to processes. It also models the kernel/user split so user programs cannot touch kernel memory. A simple bump+bitmap allocator over a page count; enough to give each process its own region. Virtual-to-physical translation is modeled as a per-process base offset. Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM.

SLMemoryModule #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLMemoryModule.sleela)

SLMemoryModule class

Defines SLMemoryModule — a selectable main-memory part a user plugs into a Sleela executor build. It carries the real-world specification of a RAM module: technology (DRAM/SDRAM/DDRn/SRAM), capacity, data-bus width, clock, CAS latency, and the resulting first-word latency and peak transfer bandwidth. The timings are what make one RAM choice faster than another; SLComponentCatalog offers presets (DDR3-1600, DDR5-6000, ...). The module backs an SLRAM at the chosen capacity; the spec fields drive the performance model (effective bandwidth, access latency) so overclocked CPUs and faster RAM visibly change an executor's characterization. Family: cpu.components. Composes SLRAM; selected via SLComponentCatalog.

SLMemoryTierRouter #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLMemoryTierRouter.sleela)

SLMemoryTierRouter class

Defines SLMemoryTierRouter — the piece that makes memory tiers PHYSICAL. A build can carry two real memory modules: a "usual" tier (for usual activities, e.g. DDR2) and an "accurate" tier (for competency/ accuracy-critical work, e.g. DDR5). This router holds both, knows the program's default (main) tier, and — given a function's declared tier — returns the actual SLMemoryModule that function should bind its memory accesses to. The VM/dispatcher consults it per function so a program marked `usualmem`/`accuratemem` (or defaulted at the document level) runs against the matching module, not a single shared store. Tier ids mirror the Sleela memory-tier modifiers and SLAccessSemantics shape: 0 = inherit (use the main tier), 1 = usual (DDR2), 2 = accurate (DDR5). A function that declares neither inherits the main tier. Family: cpu.components. Composes SLMemoryModule; held by SLExecutorBuild; consulted by the VM dispatch path.

SLMIPSCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/mips/SLMIPSCPU.sleela)

SLMIPSCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLMIPSCPU — a runnable model of a classic 32-bit MIPS R- style load/store RISC: 32 general registers (R0 hardwired to zero), the HI and LO multiply/divide result registers, and a program counter. It extends SLCPURuntime and adds the MIPS register conventions, a decoder for a compact R/I-type encoding, and the branch-delay-slot / CP0 hooks the skeleton named. Instruction model (op in bits 24..31, rd in 16..23, rs in 8..15, rt/imm in 0..7): ADD rd,rs,rt / SUB rd,rs,rt / ADDI rd,rs,imm / LW rd,imm(rs) / SW rt,imm(rs) / BEQ rs,rt,off / BNE rs,rt,off / J addr / NOP / SYSCALL(halt). R0 reads as zero and ignores writes, as on real MIPS. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLMMU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLMMU.sleela)

SLMMU class

Defines SLMMU — a Memory Management Unit providing real page-table translation from a guest's (virtual / guest-physical) address space to host-physical addresses, with per-page presence and protection bits. This is step 2 of the OS-VM roadmap: it replaces the single base-offset window with genuine second-level address translation, so a guest OS can have paged memory, unmapped regions that fault, and read-only/no-execute protections — the memory model a real kernel needs. Model: a single-level page table over a configurable page size. Each entry records the host-physical frame and permission bits (present, write, exec). translate() walks the table; a miss or protection violation raises a page fault (returned as -1 with the fault recorded), which the hypervisor delivers to the guest as a TRAP. Page-table entries are stored in SLRAM (one word per entry: frame<<3 | perms) so the table can be large (realistic address spaces). Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM.

SLMotherboard #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLMotherboard.sleela)

SLMotherboard class

Defines SLMotherboard — the board a Sleela executor is built on: the CPU socket, the platform chipset, the memory topology (channel count and DIMM slots), the number of PCIe lanes the platform exposes and their generation, and the system-bus generation the board carries. These are the "motherboard-pertinent settings" that bound a build: a CPU only drops into a matching socket, memory can only populate as many channels as the board routes, and no card can use more PCIe lanes than the platform provides. The board is nameful and spec-first: every field states a real platform property (sTR5 socket, TRX50/WRX90 chipset, 4- vs 8-channel memory, PCIe 5.0 lane budget) rather than assuming a generic machine. SLExecutorBuild mounts a board and can check that the chosen CPU socket and memory channels fit it. Family: cpu.components. Selected via SLComponentCatalog; mounted in SLExecutorBuild; partners SLMemoryModule and SLSystemBus.

SLOpcodeMap #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLOpcodeMap.sleela)

SLOpcodeMap class

Defines SLOpcodeMap — the translator that maps the register-style CPU ISA (SLInstructionSet) and the OS system calls (SLSystemCall) ONTO the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate (SLSleelaOpcode), emitting the result into an SLSleelaVM. This is the pivot of the whole design: every CPU instruction and every OS service is expressed as a sequence of canonical Sleela opcodes. Because the Sleela opcodes are Turing complete and already executed by the native VM, mapping the CPU ISA + syscalls onto them means the register machine's behavior is fully realized by the substrate. Repeating this mapping for whatever a frontend emits is exactly what makes C/C++/Java/Sleela 1:1 in Turing effect: they all become streams of the same opcodes. Register model: the register file is mapped to Sleela GLOBAL slots (rN -> global N). A register op becomes: load operands from globals, do the stack arithmetic, store the result back to a global. Family: cpu. Composes SLInstructionSet, SLSystemCall, SLSleelaOpcode, SLSleelaVM.

SLOperatingSystem #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLOperatingSystem.sleela)

SLOperatingSystem class

Defines SLOperatingSystem — the full OS assembly: it constructs the kernel and all its subsystems over a given CPU and memory, wires the standard device drivers, and exposes a clean API for the machine to boot and for programs to be loaded and run. This is the Sleela Class-Driven OS. Composition order mirrors a real boot: memory manager -> I/O bus + drivers -> filesystem -> syscalls -> scheduler -> kernel. Family: cpu. Top of the OS layer; composes SLKernel and all subsystems.

SLOpticalDrive #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLOpticalDrive.sleela)

SLOpticalDrive class

Defines SLOpticalDrive — a selectable optical drive for a Sleela executor build: CD, DVD, or Blu-ray reader/writer. It models the real spec that sets its speed: the medium, the base 1× data rate for that medium, the drive's speed multiplier (e.g. 52× CD, 16× DVD), and whether it can write. The 1× rate differs per medium (CD 150 KB/s, DVD 1,385 KB/s, BD 4,500 KB/s), so a "16×" DVD and a "16×" CD are very different throughputs — this class makes that explicit. Family: cpu.components. Selected via SLComponentCatalog.

SLPDP11CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/pdp11/SLPDP11CPU.sleela)

SLPDP11CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLPDP11CPU — a runnable model of the DEC PDP-11. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the DEC PDP-11 register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLPDP9CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/pdp9/SLPDP9CPU.sleela)

SLPDP9CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLPDP9CPU — a runnable model of the DEC PDP-9. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the DEC PDP-9 register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. SLProcess #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLProcess.sleela)

SLProcess class

Defines SLProcess — a unit of execution the OS schedules: a process control block (PCB). It records the process id, its state (new, ready, running, blocked, terminated), its saved program counter and a few saved registers (its context), its memory base, and accounting. The scheduler switches the CPU between processes by saving/restoring this. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela OS data structure.

SLRamTiming #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLRamTiming.sleela)

SLRamTiming class

Defines SLRamTiming — the expert memory-timing settings of a RAM channel, stated the way a DRAM datasheet / BIOS does: the actual data rate (MT/s), the Vddq rail, and the primary timings CL, tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tRC and command rate as CLOCK CYCLES, plus the derived nanosecond latencies those cycles cost at the dialed data rate. Rather than assume memory keeps up, each primary timing becomes a named SLTiming budget checked against the bus period, and the first-word read latency is reported in real nanoseconds. Expert knobs are explicit: an operator tightens CL/tRCD/tRP/tRAS and the class recomputes real access latency and re-checks every budget against the settled Vddq, so tightening past what the voltage honors is refused. Family: cpu. Composes SLTiming and SLVoltageRail; partners SLRAM/SLBusTiming.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

restampvoid restamp()Re-derive each budget. A primary timing of N command-clocks must physically complete inside N clock periods: the window the controller allows is N periods, and the DRAM's internal settle (modeled as the array's fixed ~ns access translated back into this period) must fit with margin. We model the settle as (N-1) periods of propagation, so a tighter N shrinks the slack — tighten too far and the budget stops being honored.

SLRegisterFile #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLRegisterFile.sleela)

Defines SLRegisterFile — the bank of general-purpose registers a CPU core reads and writes each cycle. SLRISCVCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/riscv/SLRISCVCPU.sleela)

SLRISCVCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLRISCVCPU — a runnable model of RV32I: 32 integer registers (x0 hardwired to zero), a program counter, and a small CSR file. It extends SLCPURuntime and adds the RISC-V register conventions, an immediate generator, a decoder for a compact R/I/B/J encoding, and the trap / system-instruction hooks the skeleton named. Instruction model (op in bits 24..31, rd in 16..23, rs1 in 8..15, rs2/imm in 0..7): ADD / SUB / ADDI / LW / SW / BEQ / BNE / JAL / ECALL(trap+halt) / NOP. x0 reads as zero and discards writes, matching the architecture. Compact teaching encoding, enough to run the CPU and host further .sleela inputs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLRockchipCPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/rockchip/SLRockchipCPU.sleela)

SLRockchipCPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLRockchipCPU — a runnable model of the Rockchip (ARM64). It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the Rockchip (ARM64) register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLScheduler #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLScheduler.sleela)

SLScheduler class

Defines SLScheduler — the OS component that decides which ready process runs next and for how long. This models a round-robin scheduler with a fixed time quantum: the timer interrupt preempts the running process at the end of its quantum and the scheduler rotates to the next ready one. Holds up to 8 processes (SLeeLa surface has no arrays); enough to demonstrate multiprogramming on the modeled machine. Family: cpu. Composes SLProcess.
