BASE_COUNTstatic final int BASE_COUNT = 49--- Double-shelf opcode tiers -------------------------------------------- The native substrate (impl/core/sleela_core.h `SLOp`) defines 155 opcodes (codes 0..154). All are acceptable; the tiers below do not gate execution, they let the professional monitoring/storage layer tag each opcode by the SHELF it belongs to and iterate each shelf under its own flag. The three shelves are contiguous half-open ranges [prev, COUNT): Shelf 1 codes 0..48 base computational/service core (through OP_HALT): arithmetic, control flow, call/return, threads, sockets, pipes, files. The Turing-complete subset the CPU ISA + syscalls lower onto. Shelf 2 codes 49..97 substrate extensions: time services, structs, Synchro / Munction / Best-of. Part of the canonical substrate. Shelf 3 codes 98..154 host-facing services: arrays, OS syscalls, GC hint, `ran::`, Idea realtime canvas, VM-select / Modium, UI bridge, structural send, runtime type checks, and two-entry stack duplication. end of shelf 1 (base core), exclusive
SUBSTRATE_COUNTstatic final int SUBSTRATE_COUNT = 98end of shelf 2 (substrate), exclusive
NATIVE_COUNTstatic final int NATIVE_COUNT = 155end of shelf 3 (full native enum), exclusive. Includes host-facing services through OP_DUP2 (154) OP_UI_CALL (150), OP_SSEND (151), OP_CHECKCAST (152), OP_INSTANCEOF (153), and OP_DUP2 (154): the real opcodes are 0..154, so the count is 155.
OP_UI_CALLstatic final int OP_UI_CALL = 150OP_SSEND (151): the ::: structural-offload send. A host-shelf service opcode that frames a String source element-by-element into a receiver reach.

SLSleelaVM #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLSleelaVM.sleela)

SLSleelaVM class

Defines SLSleelaVM — a stack machine that executes the canonical SLeeLa opcodes (SLSleelaOpcode) directly. It mirrors the native dispatch loop in impl/core/sleela_core.c ("in = code[ip++]; switch(in.op){...}"): fetch one opcode, execute it against an operand stack and globals, advance. This is the Turing-complete substrate of the entire CPU model. Every higher layer — the register-style SLControlUnit, the OS system calls, and all four language frontends — ultimately produces a stream of these opcodes, and this VM gives that stream its meaning. Running the same effect here and on the native VM is what makes the equivalence (SLTuringBridge) concrete. Operand stack and globals are modeled over SLRAM so arbitrarily large computations are expressible (unbounded tape => Turing-complete). Family: cpu. Composes SLSleelaOpcode, SLStack, SLRAM.

SLStack #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLStack.sleela)

SLStack class

Defines SLStack — the hardware call/data stack a core uses for PUSH/POP and for CALL/RET return addresses. It is a region of main memory addressed through a stack pointer (SP) that grows downward from a base, the classic convention on x86/ARM. The control unit drives it; the OS gives each process its own stack region. Grows downward: push decrements SP then writes; pop reads then increments. Overflow (past the limit) and underflow (past the base) are reported, not silently wrapped. Family: cpu. Composes SLRAM.

SLStorageDevice #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/components/SLStorageDevice.sleela)

SLStorageDevice class

Defines SLStorageDevice — a selectable mass-storage part for a Sleela executor build: hard disk, solid-state disk, NVMe, floppy, or tape. It carries the real spec that distinguishes them — capacity, interface (ST-506/IDE/SATA/SAS/NVMe), rotational speed (RPM, 0 for solid state), average seek time, and sequential transfer rate — plus a simple access-time model (seek + rotational latency + transfer) so a build with a fast NVMe behaves differently from one with a 3600-RPM MFM drive. Family: cpu.components. Selected via SLComponentCatalog.

SLSystemCall #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLSystemCall.sleela)

SLSystemCall class

Defines SLSystemCall — the system-call interface: the controlled doorway from user programs into the kernel. A user program issues the SYSCALL instruction with a call number; the CPU switches to supervisor mode and jumps to the kernel's syscall handler, which dispatches on the number. This class is the registry of call numbers and the dispatcher contract. Call numbers model a minimal POSIX-like surface: write, read, open, close, exit, spawn, yield. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela ABI definition.

SLTiming #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLTiming.sleela)

SLTiming class

Defines SLTiming — one named, careful timing budget: the atom all the expert bus / CPU / I/O / RAM timings are built from. A budget names a path and states its real electrical constraints in picoseconds (ps): setup, hold, propagation, and jitter, all against a declared period. Rather than assume a part is "fast enough", a budget is CHECKED — slack is period minus the consumed time, and a path is honored only when slack is non-negative with the stated guardband. Everything here is nameful and quality-first: each budget carries the signal name and a human reason, so a timing report reads as prose, not as magic numbers. A compiled .sleela file embeds these budgets so a compiler or VM operates the STATED timings instead of inferring confidences about silicon. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela timing model (picosecond integer arithmetic).

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLTimingManifest #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLTimingManifest.sleela)

SLTimingManifest class

Defines SLTimingManifest — the compact, serializable record of a timing/voltage/expertise profile that a COMPILED .sleela file carries inside it. This is the pivot the request turns on: a compiled program must not oblige a compiler or VM to GUESS the quality of the hardware it runs on ("rather than inherently to expect the quality of these operating as confidences of how CPUs operate"). Instead the program states its timings, and the engine operates those STATED numbers. A manifest flattens an SLTimingProfile into plain integers/strings: the expertise tier + brand/medium, the dialed core/bus/io clocks, the settled rail voltages, the RAM primaries, and the worst honored slack. It can be embedded as a header in an SLProgram image and read back by any consumer — SLSleelaVM, SLControlUnit, SLCompilerDriver — so every stage honors the same declared operating point. Family: cpu. Serialization layer over SLTimingProfile; embedded in SLProgram.

SLTMS320CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/tms320/SLTMS320CPU.sleela)

SLTMS320CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLTMS320CPU — a runnable model of the TI TMS320. It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the TI TMS320 register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLVoltageRail #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLVoltageRail.sleela)

SLVoltageRail class

Defines SLVoltageRail — one adjustable supply rail with ACTUAL voltages expressed in millivolts (mV). A real CPU, its buses, its I/O ring, and its memory each sit on named rails (Vcore, Vsoc, Vddq, Vio, ...). The rail carries a nominal operating point, hard floor/ceiling limits, a per-rail load-line droop (how far the voltage sags under current), and an offset the operator dials in. The settled voltage a timing budget must survive is `effective()` = nominal + offset - droopAtLoad. Voltages are kept careful and nameful: every rail has a name, a reason for its limits, and a settle point you can read back and reason about. Nothing here assumes a "confidence" about how a part behaves — it states the actual electrical operating point the timings below are proven against. Family: cpu. Pure Sleela electrical model (millivolt integer arithmetic).

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

ceilingMvint ceilingMvhard upper limit; above this the part is unsafe

SLWorkload #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/SLWorkload.sleela)

SLWorkload class

Defines SLWorkload — a unit of work to run on a CPU, written in C, C++, or Sleela (and Java, which shares the same frontend path). A workload names its source, its language, and the SLCPUResource grant it needs. compile() drives the shared multi-language pipeline (SLCompilerDriver -> SLProgram, the register-ISA image); the CPU then maps that image onto its own canonical-opcode substrate and runs it inside the grant. The SAME workload therefore runs identically whether its source was C, C++, or Sleela — the 1:1 Turing-effect guarantee (SLTuringBridge). Family: cpu. Composes SLCPUResource, SLCompilerDriver, SLProgram; consumed by SLCPURuntime.runWorkload().

SLX86CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/x86/SLX86CPU.sleela)

SLX86CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLX86CPU — a runnable model of a 32-bit x86 (IA-32 style): the general registers EAX ECX EDX EBX ESP EBP ESI EDI, an EFLAGS register, and a program counter (EIP). It extends SLCPURuntime and adds the x86 register set, a decoder for a compact two-operand encoding, the protected- mode / control-register and interrupt hooks the skeleton named, and — as a worked example of a CPU running ON TOP OF the secondary Sleela VM — a lower() path that translates a short x86 sequence into canonical opcodes and executes them on the inherited SLSleelaVM substrate. Instruction model (op in high byte, 4-bit dst + 4-bit src/imm in low byte): MOV r,imm / MOV r,r / ADD r,r / SUB r,r / INC r / CMP r,r / MOV r,[m] / MOV [m],r / JMP / JE / JNE / INT(interrupt+halt) / HLT / NOP. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

It extends SLCPURuntime, so it inherits register storage, a word-addressable memory interface, an SLALU, the fetch-decode-execute loop, and — crucially — the resource-aware workload path (admit()/runWorkload()) that runs C, C++ or Sleela programs on this CPU within an SLCPUResource grant, mapped onto the canonical SLeeLa opcode substrate. This file supplies the Xbox One (x86-64 Jaguar) register set and a decode() over a compact instruction encoding (load/move/arithmetic/compare/branch/halt). It is a functional model sufficient to run the CPU as a CPU and as a target for further .sleela inputs, not a cycle-accurate emulator; per-arch bus/timing detail remains in this folder's markdown docs. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

SLZ80CPU #sleela 2.5 (lib/cpu/z80/SLZ80CPU.sleela)

SLZ80CPU class extends SLCPURuntime

Defines SLZ80CPU — a runnable model of the Zilog Z80: an 8-bit machine with the A accumulator, B/C/D/E/H/L general registers, a 16-bit stack pointer, an R refresh register, and S Z H PV N C flags. It extends SLCPURuntime for register/memory/ALU/loop machinery and adds the Z80 register set, a decoder, a separate I/O port space, and the refresh/wait behaviours the skeleton named. Instruction model (op in high byte, operand in low byte of each word): a compact teaching encoding sufficient to run the CPU and host further .sleela inputs — LD r,n / LD A,(nn) / LD (nn),A / ADD A,n / SUB n / INC r / OUT (n),A / IN A,(n) / JP nn / JR Z,e / JR NZ,e / HALT / NOP. Family: cpu. Extends SLCPURuntime.

admitboolean admit(Workload w)Admission: the workload fits only if its memory request fits this CPU's address space and the grant has a positive budget.
runWorkloadint runWorkload(Workload w)Run a workload within its grant. Charges the instruction cost (clamped to the budget) and returns a deterministic observable output: the workload's base result, identical across architectures (the 1:1 Turing-effect guarantee), independent of clock. Returns -1 if rejected.
